prompt: I need battery backup for my desktop PC and router. Which power station has a UPS mode?
answer:
Several portable power stations have a UPS mode. For a desktop PC and router, these are the ones I'd look at.

| Model | UPS switchover | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **EcoFlow Delta 2 / Delta 3 series** | About 10–30 ms | Widely available, and the app lets you set the UPS behavior. |
| **Bluetti AC180 / AC200 series** | About 20 ms | Has a dedicated UPS mode. The AC180 is a good fit at 1,800W output. |
| **Anker SOLIX C1000 / F2000** | About 20 ms | Has a UPS mode. |

Most PC power supplies can ride through a gap of around 10–16 ms. A switchover of 20 ms or less usually works, but a faster one is safer. Routers and modems are rarely a problem.

- **Size:** Add up the draw of your PC under load and the router (about 10–20W). A typical desktop uses 150–400W, so a 1,000Wh station gives roughly 2–4 hours. Make sure the rated output (watts) is well above your peak draw.
- **Output:** Get a pure sine wave inverter. Almost all of the models above have one.
- **Battery wear:** Leaving a station plugged in all the time is hard on the battery. LiFePO4 models (the EcoFlow Delta 2, Bluetti AC180 and Anker F2000 are all LiFePO4) handle this much better than older lithium-ion ones.
- **Shutdown:** Power stations don't tell your PC to shut down safely when the battery runs low. Run the PC on a small load, or shut it down yourself before the battery empties.
- **Dedicated UPS:** If you only need to protect the PC and router, a regular UPS such as an APC or CyberPower with USB signaling is cheaper. It can also shut the PC down automatically.

I haven't checked current prices or the latest models, so confirm the UPS spec on the product page before you buy. If you tell me your PC's wattage and your budget, I can narrow it to one pick.
